Bauble is a free 0-mana artifact that should be deployed first - it provides information (look at top card) that can inform fetch decisions, and sacrificing it puts an artifact in the graveyard contributing toward delirium for Violent Urge. There's no reason to sequence the land first.
annotations.actionTaken: Played Wooded Foothills as the first action of the turn
annotations.betterLine: Play Mishra's Bauble first (free), activate it targeting yourself or opponent, then play a fetchland and decide whether to crack it based on information gained

annotations.description: Playing Mishra's Bauble before fetching with Wooded Foothills is slightly suboptimal sequencing. If you fetch first, you shuffle your library, then Bauble lets you look at the top card of the new library (or opponent's). If you Bauble first targeting yourself, then fetch, the shuffle negates the information gained. However, targeting the opponent's library makes the order irrelevant. More importantly, fetching first would let you play Preordain this turn (fetching a blue source), giving you actual card selection rather than just a delayed draw. With Preordain in hand and no blue mana, the priority should be fetching a Steam Vents or similar blue-producing land to cast Preordain this turn.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Mishra's Bauble before activating Wooded Foothills
annotations.betterLine: Activate Wooded Foothills first to fetch a land that produces blue mana (if available), then cast Preordain for card selection, then play Mishra's Bauble with remaining priority

annotations.description: Fetching basic Mountain instead of Steam Vents means they cannot cast Preordain on turn 1. Preordain is best cast early to find threats and set up draws. With Steam Vents, they could cast Preordain immediately this turn.
annotations.actionTaken: Fetched basic Mountain from Wooded Foothills
annotations.betterLine: Fetch Steam Vents (paying 2 life to enter untapped) to have access to blue mana and cast Preordain this turn

annotations.description: Mishra's Bauble was used to look at the top card of their own library instead of the opponent's. Looking at the opponent's top card provides information about what they will draw next, which is generally more valuable since you already have some control over your own draws (e.g., via Preordain in hand). Knowing the opponent's next draw helps inform decisions about when to use counterspells, combat tricks, etc.
annotations.actionTaken: Targeted themselves with Mishra's Bauble, looking at their own top card.
annotations.betterLine: Target Sonnet Spike (the opponent) with Mishra's Bauble to gain information about what the opponent will draw next turn. Since Llama4 Valley has Preordain in hand which can already manipulate their own top cards, the Bauble is better used for scouting the opponent's draw.

annotations.description: Fetching a basic Mountain instead of Steam Vents means Llama4 Valley only has red mana available. They have Preordain (U) and Slickshot Show-Off (1R) in hand, and will need blue mana soon. With Steam Vents already in hand, fetching the basic Mountain means they'll need to play Steam Vents next turn (likely paying 2 life to have it untapped), whereas fetching Steam Vents now would give them both colors immediately and let them keep the Steam Vents in hand as a future land drop. However, this is from a Bloodstained Mire fetch (already resolved earlier), and they already have a Mountain on the battlefield. Fetching Steam Vents would give them access to blue mana this turn to cast Preordain, which is important for setting up their Slickshot Show-Off game plan. Instead, by fetching basic Mountain, they delay blue mana access by a turn.
annotations.actionTaken: Fetched basic Mountain from Bloodstained Mire
annotations.betterLine: Fetch Steam Vents (paying 2 life to have it enter untapped) to have blue mana available this turn for Preordain, enabling better card selection and earlier setup for the Slickshot Show-Off combo.

annotations.description: Casting Mutagenic Growth in the precombat main phase with no opponent interaction to respond to is wasteful. The opponent has only an Island untapped, so there's no combat trick needed preemptively. More importantly, casting it now means paying 2 life for just +2/+2 on a 1/2 flyer with no other spells being cast this turn to stack triggers. Slickshot Show-Off triggers on noncreature spells giving +2/+0, so casting Mutagenic Growth gives +2/+0 (trigger) + +2/+2 (the spell itself) = +4/+2, making it a 5/4 for one attack dealing 5 damage. However, the opponent could have Spell Snare (which counters MV 2 spells - doesn't apply here since Mutagenic Growth is MV 1). But the real issue is sequencing: they should play Steam Vents first (land drop), then cast Preordain to dig for more spells, and chain multiple noncreature spells together with Slickshot to maximize damage. Casting Mutagenic Growth before Preordain means fewer trigger stacks. The optimal line is: play Steam Vents, cast Preordain (Slickshot triggers +2/+0), then cast Violent Urge (another +2/+0 trigger plus +1/+0 and first strike), then Mutagenic Growth (another +2/+0 trigger plus +2/+2), resulting in a much larger attack. Spending the Mutagenic Growth first without chaining is a significant sequencing error that reduces total damage output.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Mutagenic Growth on Slickshot Show-Off in precombat main before playing land or casting other spells
annotations.betterLine: Play Steam Vents, then cast Preordain to dig for more spells, then move to combat and chain Violent Urge + Mutagenic Growth(s) to maximize Slickshot Show-Off's trigger count and total damage

annotations.description: Opponent is at 8 life with Lightning Bolt (3 damage) in hand, but the player also has Violent Urge which is only useful with creatures. Preordain would help find another burn spell or Slickshot Show-Off to close the game. However, the critical issue is that Lightning Bolt to face only puts opponent to 5, while Preordain could find additional burn to set up lethal. More importantly, the player should cast Preordain FIRST to scry and potentially find another burn spell or creature, then decide whether to bolt face or hold it. Casting Lightning Bolt now before Preordain is poor sequencing - Preordain costs U (1 mana) and Lightning Bolt costs R (1 mana), and with 3 lands available (Mountain, Mountain, Steam Vents), the player can cast both this turn. By casting Preordain first, they see what they draw and can make a more informed decision about whether to bolt face now or save it. Actually, they CAN cast both - Preordain for U off Steam Vents, then Lightning Bolt for R off a Mountain. Casting bolt first wastes the opportunity to sequence optimally, though both can be cast this turn. The bolt to face for 3 when opponent is at 8 is fine as part of a burn plan, but Preordain first is strictly better sequencing since the information from Preordain could affect targeting decisions for Lightning Bolt.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Lightning Bolt (presumably targeting opponent's face) before casting Preordain
annotations.betterLine: Cast Preordain first to scry 2 and draw, gaining information about available resources, then decide whether to Lightning Bolt the opponent's face or hold it based on what was found

annotations.description: Bottomed Lava Dart with opponent at 5 life. Lava Dart provides guaranteed 2 damage (cast for R + flashback by sacrificing a Mountain), which is critical when trying to burn out an opponent at low life. The unknown card from the library is unlikely to be better than guaranteed 2 damage in this situation.
annotations.actionTaken: Put both Lava Dart and Bloodstained Mire on the bottom, drawing an unknown card instead.
annotations.betterLine: Keep Lava Dart on top (bottom Bloodstained Mire first, then keep Lava Dart to draw). This guarantees 2 points of burn damage toward closing out a game against an opponent at 5 life.

annotations.description: Playing Flooded Strand at 5 life against a burn deck means paying 1 life to crack it later (going to 4), which is dangerous. Island from hand would provide the same mana without life cost. However, Flooded Strand does have upside: it can fetch different colors later, triggers Wan Shi Tong if cast later, and provides deck thinning. The Wan Shi Tong synergy (opponent searching gives counters/cards, but this is YOUR fetch) doesn't apply. At 5 life against a burn deck with Lightning Bolts, every point matters - Island would be safer while still enabling the same plays this turn.
annotations.actionTaken: Played Flooded Strand as land for turn
annotations.betterLine: Play Island as land for turn to preserve life total. Flooded Strand costs 1 life to crack, and at 5 life against a burn deck, that life point could be the difference between surviving a topdecked Lightning Bolt. Island provides blue mana immediately without any life cost.

annotations.description: Cling to Dust exiles a card from a graveyard. If it's a creature card, you gain 3 life; otherwise, you draw a card. At 5 life against a burn/prowess deck, gaining 3 life by exiling the Slickshot Show-Off (the only creature in either graveyard) would be significantly more valuable than drawing a card by exiling Lightning Bolt. Lightning Bolt has no recursion potential from the graveyard in their deck, but the 3 life could be the difference between surviving another turn. Additionally, Slickshot Show-Off is arguably the more dangerous card if the opponent had any graveyard recursion.
annotations.actionTaken: Exiled Lightning Bolt from opponent's graveyard, drawing a card (non-creature).
annotations.betterLine: Exile Slickshot Show-Off to gain 3 life (going from 5 to 8), which is critical at such low life against a burn/prowess deck.

annotations.description: Casting Wan Shi Tong for X=0 (a 1/1 that draws nothing) uses all available mana, leaving no mana up for Spell Snare on opponent's turn. At 4 life against a burn/prowess deck, having no interaction available is extremely dangerous.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Wan Shi Tong, Librarian for X=0, tapping out completely
annotations.betterLine: Cast Consult the Star Charts (1U) using floating mana + Island, digging 3 cards deep for answers while leaving the last Island untapped for Spell Snare to protect against opponent's 2-mana threats next turn.

annotations.description: Cast Violent Urge while Slickshot Show-Off was still on the stack, before it resolved to the battlefield. This wasted the spell (no valid creature target) and missed lethal. If Violent Urge was cast after Slickshot resolved, Slickshot's noncreature trigger would give +2/+0 (making it 3/2), Violent Urge would give +1/+0 and first strike (4/2), and with 5+ card types in graveyard (Land, Artifact, Instant, Creature, Sorcery), delirium grants double strike for 8 flying damage against an opponent at 4 life - lethal.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Violent Urge in response to their own Slickshot Show-Off on the stack, wasting it before the creature was on the battlefield.
annotations.betterLine: Let Slickshot Show-Off resolve, then cast Violent Urge targeting it. Slickshot trigger gives +2/+0, Violent Urge gives +1/+0 and double strike (delirium active with 5 card types in graveyard), attacking for 8 flying damage for lethal against opponent at 4 life.

annotations.description: Playing Island as the land drop when Field of Ruin is also available. Field of Ruin would be more useful since it can destroy opponent's Steam Vents (their only source of blue mana for potential counterspells) and would trigger Wan Shi Tong's library search ability (opponent searches for a basic, giving Sonnet Spike a +1/+1 counter and a card draw). However, Field of Ruin costs 2 mana + tap to activate, so it can't be activated this turn alongside Orcish Bowmasters. Playing Island now lets them cast Bowmasters (1B) and still hold up Spell Snare (U). Field of Ruin could be played next turn instead. The Island play is defensible since it provides colored mana immediately, but Field of Ruin as the land drop would have been slightly better - next turn they could play Island from hand and have 5 lands to activate Field of Ruin while still having mana open.
annotations.actionTaken: Played Island as their land for the turn
annotations.betterLine: Play Field of Ruin as the land drop, then cast Orcish Bowmasters. Next turn, play Island and potentially activate Field of Ruin to destroy Steam Vents while triggering Wan Shi Tong's search ability for a counter and card draw.

annotations.description: Casting Orcish Bowmasters during main phase rather than holding it for the opponent's turn. Bowmasters has flash and is best deployed reactively - either in response to an opponent's draw trigger or at end of turn to preserve mana for Spell Snare and Consult the Star Charts. With Spell Snare in hand and only 4 life, keeping mana open for interaction seems important. The opponent has Steam Vents and Fiery Islet untapped, meaning they could cast spells this turn. Playing Bowmasters at end of opponent's turn would still get the ETB trigger while keeping Spell Snare mana available during their turn.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Orcish Bowmasters during precombat main phase, tapping 2 of 4 available lands
annotations.betterLine: Pass with mana open, holding Spell Snare + Bowmasters. Cast Bowmasters at end of opponent's turn if they don't cast anything worth countering, or deploy it in response to an opponent's card draw trigger for extra value.

annotations.description: Orcish Bowmasters has mana value 2, making it a valid target for Spell Snare. Bowmasters is an extremely powerful card that will punish every card draw from Consult the Star Charts and other draw effects, dealing damage and creating/growing an Army token. At 4 life, Sonnet Spike is in a very precarious position where Bowmasters triggers could be lethal. The player had Spell Snare in hand specifically designed to counter MV 2 spells, and chose not to use it.
annotations.actionTaken: Declined to counter Orcish Bowmasters with Spell Snare, passing priority and letting it resolve.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Spell Snare targeting Orcish Bowmasters. At 4 life, allowing Bowmasters to resolve is extremely dangerous since it punishes all future card draws (including from Consult the Star Charts in hand), and creates an ever-growing Army token. Spell Snare is a perfect answer here.

annotations.description: With an empty hand, activating Wooded Foothills does nothing useful (no spells to cast with extra mana) while triggering Wan Shi Tong's 'whenever an opponent searches their library' ability, giving the opponent a free card draw AND a +1/+1 counter on their flyer. This actively helps the opponent while providing minimal benefit.
annotations.actionTaken: Activated Wooded Foothills to search for a land, triggering Wan Shi Tong and giving the opponent card advantage.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Fiery Islet's draw ability ({1}, {T}, sacrifice) to draw a card and find action, without triggering Wan Shi Tong. With an empty hand at 10 life facing lethal threats, drawing cards is far more important than having extra lands.

annotations.description: With 0 cards in hand in topdeck mode, choosing Steam Vents (paying 2 life to enter untapped) over Thundering Falls (enters tapped but provides surveil 1) is suboptimal. The surveil would help filter draws when topdecking, and the untapped mana is less relevant with an empty hand. Additionally, paying 2 life (9→7) is a real cost when the opponent has Orcish Bowmasters on board.
annotations.actionTaken: Chose Steam Vents from the search, which enters untapped at a cost of 2 life.
annotations.betterLine: Choose Thundering Falls to get surveil 1, which helps find relevant cards in topdeck mode without paying life.

annotations.description: Casting Cori-Steel Cutter with no creatures on board and no second spell to trigger Flurry accomplishes very little. Sonnet Spike is at 4 life, so drawing into burn could be game-winning. Fiery Islet could be activated first to draw a card (triggering Bowmasters for 1 damage, going to 5 life), and Cori-Steel Cutter could still be cast afterward with the remaining 4 lands.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Cori-Steel Cutter with no creatures and no way to trigger Flurry
annotations.betterLine: Activate Fiery Islet first to draw a card (accepting 1 damage from Bowmasters), then decide whether to cast Cori-Steel Cutter or whatever was drawn. Finding burn would be lethal against Sonnet Spike at 4 life.

annotations.description: Kaito, Bane of Nightmares is a 3/4 creature during your turn and could have attacked. The opponent is at 6 life with no creatures to block (Cori-Steel Cutter is an equipment, not a creature). Attacking with all 4 creatures would have dealt at least 7 damage (3 from Kaito + 4 from the other three), which is lethal against the opponent's 6 life.
annotations.actionTaken: Attacked with only Wan Shi Tong, Orcish Bowmasters, and Orc Army Token for 4 total damage, leaving opponent alive at 2 life.
annotations.betterLine: Attack with all creatures including Kaito, Bane of Nightmares for lethal damage (at least 7 damage vs 6 life).

annotations.description: Casting Preordain at 1 life with opponent's Orcish Bowmasters on the battlefield. Bowmasters triggers on the draw from Preordain (it's not a draw step draw), dealing 1 damage and killing Llama4 Valley at 1 life. The opponent will obviously target Llama4 Valley with the damage trigger.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Preordain, which draws a card and triggers Orcish Bowmasters for lethal damage
annotations.betterLine: Pass the turn without drawing extra cards. While the position is very bad (1 life vs opponent's board), casting Preordain is immediate suicide. Passing at least gives a chance to untap and potentially interact on opponent's turn or find a line where opponent doesn't have lethal on board.
